svg.title: Natural-language search in Deal4Me: ask in any language, code checks the price
svg.desc: Animated three-stage diagram that loops through two buyer queries. Stage 1, the ask: a buyer's query bubble with a microphone glyph (voice or text, any language), first in Japanese, スキー板を3日間借りたい。予算は150ドル, then in English, I need skis for 3 days under $150, sent to POST /api/ai/search. Stage 2, Claude Haiku, parse only: Haiku turns the request into a structured filter whose fields appear one by one: kind rental, keywords ski, rentalDays 3, maxPrice $150, budgetPeriod total, lang ja (en for the English query), and matchingItemIds. The output follows a JSON schema and is re-checked with zod; the filter is cached per query, catalog and day. Stage 3, code filter on the live catalog: rules tick on one by one: published shops only; 3 days times the daily fee must be at most $150 (the highlighted key rule, at most $50 a day); the rental must allow 3 or more days; items available for the requested dates and size sort first; the owner's floor price is stripped from every result; top 6 results. Results: Skis at $35 a day, $105 for 3 days, fits; Ski and boot set at $45 a day, $135 for 3 days, fits; Performance skis at $60 a day, $180 for 3 days, is struck through as over budget. A summary returns to the buyer in the query's language: 予算内のレンタルが2件見つかりました。 for Japanese, Found 2 rentals that fit your budget for English; Haiku writes the sentence and code fills in the count.

text.font-family: 'Public Sans', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
